note: The first rig that is real. One par and one beam moving head, bought 10 Sept, driven over Art-Net through a node. Every number here is PROVISIONAL until Renjith sends the measured positions and Alnas finishes reading the personality off the fixtures -- the ones that were guessed are marked in `measured`. Zero photons ended here.

measured.par_mode: reported by eye, not read from the menu
measured.note: Correct on /live and save. Nothing here is a measurement yet.

limits.note: The head can physically move much faster than these figures. They are the limits we CHOOSE, because a beam that snaps reads as a fault and a beam that arrives reads as a gesture. pan/tilt rates are guesses until smooth.js is run against the real head; they were never measurable before today.

fixtures.note: Renjith says 3-channel. In 3-channel there is NO master dimmer -- level has to be carried inside r, g and b, which is what the frame already does (the recipe multiplies colour by level before it leaves). So dim is 0 here, meaning 'this fixture has no such channel'. If it turns out to have a dimmer and it is left at 0, nothing will light and it will look like our bug.

fixtures.model: beam moving head, sharpy type (model unconfirmed)
fixtures.hue_note: A beam head of this type almost always has a COLOUR WHEEL, not RGB mixing -- discrete slots, not a continuum. Until the personality is read, treat hue as unavailable rather than guessing a continuous mix.
fixtures.note: Its display read 002 in the photo. A 3-channel par at address 1 occupies 1-3, so a head starting at 2 OVERLAPS it and both fixtures fight. Moved to 11 here; the head's own menu must be changed to match. Channel meanings are guesses until the walk is done -- pan and tilt are the only ones that make it move, so they are the two worth guessing.
